specPoints.text: understand the effects on crop yield of increased carbon dioxide and increased temperature in glasshouses

primer.text: Three dials govern how fast a crop photosynthesises: temperature, light intensity and carbon dioxide concentration. This note explains what happens when each dial is turned up, why every dial eventually hits a ceiling, and how glasshouse growers exploit that knowledge to lift crop yields.

lessons.title: Three Dials That Decide the Harvest
sourceHeadings: Crop Plants: Increasing Carbon Dioxide & Temperature
lessons.opening: A plant with unlimited light, carbon dioxide and warmth would photosynthesise as fast as its chemistry allows, but real crops always run short of one input. Whatever is scarcest caps the rate, so raising temperature, light intensity or carbon dioxide concentration lifts photosynthesis — until another factor becomes the bottleneck.
keyPoints: Temperature, light intensity and carbon dioxide concentration are the three main limiting factors for photosynthesis.
Warming raises the rate because enzymes drive the reaction, but beyond a ceiling the enzymes denature and the rate collapses.
Brighter light speeds photosynthesis until some other input runs short.
Extra carbon dioxide accelerates the reaction because it is a raw material, again until another factor limits.

low.restatement: More warmth, more light, more carbon dioxide — each speeds the plant up until something else runs out.
low.analogy: Three taps feeding one bucket: the slowest tap decides the flow, and opening one tap only helps while it stays the slowest.
low.examPointer: Say what happens past the temperature ceiling — enzymes denature — because that turn of the curve earns the second mark.

medium.restatement: Photosynthesis is capped by whichever input is scarcest; raising temperature speeds the enzyme-driven reaction until denaturation reverses the trend, while increasing light intensity or carbon dioxide concentration raises the rate until a different factor becomes limiting in turn.
medium.analogy: A relay team whose slowest runner sets the pace; swapping in a faster runner helps only until another runner becomes the slowest.
medium.examPointer: For glasshouse questions, connect each factor to a control: heaters for temperature, lamps for light, carbon dioxide enrichment for concentration.

check.stem: Which three factors most often limit the rate of photosynthesis in a crop?

options.text: Temperature, light intensity and carbon dioxide concentration
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.

options.text: Soil pH, wind speed and humidity
options.explanation: Those affect plants, but the taught trio is different.

options.text: Water depth, salinity and pressure
options.explanation: Aquatic conditions are not the crop factors here.

options.text: Potassium, phosphate and calcium levels
options.explanation: Those are mineral ions, not the photosynthesis limiters.

check.stem: What happens to photosynthesis as temperature climbs past a certain point?

options.text: The rate falls because the enzymes controlling the reaction denature
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.

options.text: The rate keeps climbing without limit
options.explanation: Denaturation reverses the trend.

options.text: The rate stays exactly the same
options.explanation: The curve turns downward past the optimum.

options.text: The plant switches to darkness chemistry
options.explanation: No such switch occurs.

check.stem: Why does raising carbon dioxide concentration speed up photosynthesis?

options.text: Carbon dioxide is a raw material the reaction consumes
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.

options.text: Carbon dioxide warms the leaf directly
options.explanation: Any warming is separate from the raw-material role.

options.text: It gives the enzymes extra energy
options.explanation: Enzymes are not fuelled by carbon dioxide.

options.text: It replaces the need for light
options.explanation: Light remains a separate requirement.

check.stem: Light intensity on a crop is doubled, yet the rate barely moves. What does that reveal?

options.text: Some other factor is now limiting the rate
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

options.text: The light meter is broken
options.explanation: The plateau signals a different bottleneck.

options.text: The plant has stopped photosynthesising
options.explanation: The rate continues, just uncapped by light.

options.text: Extra light always poisons leaves
options.explanation: Light does not poison; scarcity elsewhere caps the rate.

check.stem: A glasshouse on a cold dull morning gets heaters and lamps switched on. Which input still caps the rate?

options.text: Whichever of temperature, light or carbon dioxide remains scarcest after the changes
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.

options.text: Soil temperature alone from then on
options.explanation: Soil temperature is not one of the three.

options.text: Nothing can ever limit again
options.explanation: Some factor always sets the ceiling.

options.text: The growers' electricity supply
options.explanation: That is a cost issue, not a plant factor.

check.stem: State the term for the factor in shortest supply that caps photosynthesis.
check.modelAnswer: The limiting factor is the scarcest input, and it sets the ceiling on the rate of photosynthesis.

check.stem: Name the raw material gases that a glasshouse enriches to speed photosynthesis.
check.modelAnswer: Carbon dioxide is enriched in the glasshouse air so photosynthesis can proceed faster.

check.stem: Explain why warming helps a cool crop only up to a point.
check.modelAnswer: Enzymes drive photosynthesis, so moderate warming raises their activity, but past the optimum their working surfaces denature and the rate drops sharply.

check.stem: A tomato grower already provides bright light and warm air. Recommend the next control to raise yield.
check.modelAnswer: Enrich the air with carbon dioxide, because with light and temperature already high that is the factor most likely to be limiting photosynthesis.

glossary.definition: Whatever input is scarcest, capping the rate of photosynthesis at that moment.
The permanent shape change that destroys an enzyme's working surface at high temperature.
How bright the light falling on a leaf is.
